consumers.notes: ShiftingVerificationHandler.HandleEvent filters source.module=counts + source.ref_type=shifting_event and calls Repository.ApplyVerifiedShiftingEvent (legacy method name), which marks verification_state='verified' only. Under the maintainer-2026-07-28 rule, Park Head approval + operator completion already own relocation/count; verifier approval cannot move or roll back census truth. A pre-000049 authorized+completed row may be lazily applied once for rollout compatibility.

Filters source.module=milk_preparation + ref_type=milk_preparation_completion. APPROVE is the only transition from pending_verification to completed for the farm-day preparation; the operator's two/five-video submit never completes it. NO FEED-STOCK FAN-OUT, deliberately (maintainer decision 2026-08-27, migration 000216; the 2026-08-22 recorder seam was removed 2026-09-02). UHT Milk stock depletes from the preparation itself, on SUBMIT, through the feed_effective_external_consumption view, which reads milk_preparation_completions directly. The retired countsapp.MilkPreparationUHTRecorder seam wrote a SECOND row into feed_external_consumption on approve, keyed at preparation_date while the view books the same milk at feeding_date (= preparation_date + 1, a DB CHECK), so the ledger row was never suppressed by its own preparation and the litres were deducted twice on any day whose previous day carried no preparation. Migration 000241 additionally suppresses a ledger row on EITHER of a preparation's dates. Pinned by TestKernelStory_UhtMilkStockDepletesOnce.

Filters source.module=milk_feeding + ref_type=milk_feeding_completion. APPROVE completes exactly one farm x feeding_date x session task and applies that accepted session's watchlist answers; two consecutive accepted Yes answers graduate a kid, while No resets the streak.

FeedDistributionVerificationHandler.HandleEvent filters source.module=feed + source.ref_type=feed_distribution_completion and calls DistributionCompletionStore.ApplyVerifiedDistribution, which flips the feed_distribution_completions row 'pending_verification' -> 'completed' and emits feed.distribution.completed. Maintainer-2026-07-26 gate, EXTENDED 2026-08-11: a feed-direction session is completed only when a verifier approves the operator's THREE proofs -- a feed-weight PHOTO, a feed-distribution VIDEO and a water-distribution VIDEO (water was photo-or-video until then; migration 000151 adds feed_weight_proof_ref). All three ride ONE verification item in capture order. Separate NEW table; the old instant feed_direction_session_completions / feed.direction.completed path is inert.

FeedPackingVerificationHandler.HandleEvent filters source.module=feed + source.ref_type=feed_packing_completion (distinct from the distribution handler, which shares module=feed but uses ref_type=feed_distribution_completion) and calls PackingCompletionStore.ApplyVerifiedPacking, which flips the feed_packing_completions row 'pending_verification' -> 'completed' and emits feed.packing.completed. Maintainer-2026-07-26 gate (SUPERSEDING the earlier 'packing stays instant' rule): a feed PACKING session is completed only when a verifier approves the operator's ONE mandatory packing video. Separate NEW table.

FeedWastageVerificationHandler.HandleEvent filters source.module=feed + source.ref_type=feed_wastage_completion (distinct from the distribution/packing/transport handlers, which share module=feed) and calls WastageCompletionStore.ApplyVerifiedWastage, which flips the feed_wastage_completions row 'pending_verification' -> 'completed' and emits feed.wastage.completed. Maintainer-2026-08-18 gate: a pen-day's wastage task (EXPERIMENT pens only, one mandatory leftover-feed video) is completed only at verifier approval; the verifier's measured leftover kg rides her own producer route (POST /feed-direction/wastage/{completion_id}/measurement) and never the verdict payload.

DeathVerificationHandler filters source.module=counts + ref_type=workflow_death_signoff and closes the death review gate. BirthVerificationHandler filters ref_type=workflow_birth_action, whose ref_id is ONE recorded birth step (action_id), and completes only that step (tasks.ApplyBirthStepVerdict); birth evidence is reviewed per recorded step (maintainer decision 2026-09-16), one item per clip the moment it is recorded, keyed counts-birth-step:<action>:r<row_version>:<proofs> so retries deduplicate and re-shoots create a fresh item. The retired ref_type=workflow_birth_signoff (one bundle per finished mother/child track) is still consumed for pre-cutover items only. Death carries two proofs in one item keyed on workflow, review round and proof refs.

VerificationVerdictHandler filters source.module=weighing + source.ref_type in (weighing_observation, weighing_shed_observation) and calls weighingpg.ApplyVerificationVerdict, the SINGLE writer of the verdict's effect on the observation (approved -> verification_status='verified'; rework -> 'rework', slot withdrawn, bucket + work items reactivated). Idempotent on the verification event id. APPLY-RECEIPT (W-18): after that transaction commits the handler calls verification MarkVerdictApplied via weighing/adapters/verificationbridge, stamping verification_items.applied_at/applied_by_module. That ack publishes NO event by design -- it is the END of the chain, not a new fact, and minting a consumer-less event is the very silent drop this registry exists to prevent. Until the ack lands the item reads as domain.VerdictStateApplying ('decided, not yet in effect') instead of vanishing out of the pending queue, so a stopped relay or dead-lettered verdict is visible rather than looking like completed work. Approval deliberately does NOT close the bucket: close is a separate WeighingMonitor leadership action (CloseScope) that approval merely UNBLOCKS via the close gate.

PCCareVerificationHandler.HandleEvent filters source.module=pc_care + source.ref_type=pc_care_task and calls ApplyVerifiedTask (approved: task 'pending_verification' -> 'completed' on both state columns, emits pc_care.task.completed) or BounceTaskForRework (rework: -> 'rework' with the verifier's reason). Registered in eventwiring.RegisterVerificationAppliers, the single shared registration point.

HealthVerificationHandler.HandleEvent filters source.module=health + source.ref_type=health_treatment_session and stamps verified_by/verified_at on the completed session (post-task evidence review; completion is never gated on the verdict).

PenReconciliationVerificationHandler.HandleEvent filters source.module=counts + source.ref_type=pen_reconciliation_card and calls ApplyVerifiedPenReconciliation, flipping the card 'pending_verification' -> 'completed'. The verifier's verdict is the ONLY gate (no approver step, maintainer decision 2026-09-02) and it never rewrites the herd register -- the register was already truth. Registered in eventwiring.RegisterVerificationAppliers.

events.producer: procurement feed-purchase delivery transaction (RecordFeedPurchaseDelivery on the purchased -> reached transition, or CreateFeedPurchase when the record form already carries the arrival date): the outbox emit rides the same transaction as the state flip that makes the load stock, so a committed arrival always announces the load exactly once and a rolled-back one never does. Maintainer decision 2026-09-03: recording a purchase no longer emits anything -- the feed is still on the road.

consumers.notes: Creates the load's aflatoxin strip-test task (round 1) idempotently on (tenant_id, feed_purchase_id, round_no); an event replay is a no-op, never a second task. Maintainer decision 2026-08-25: one toxin test per purchased feed load; review is CEO/CXO-only outside the generic Verification module. 2026-09-03: born when the load REACHES, not when it is bought.

FeedPurchaseReachedWorkflowHandler completes the feed purchase workflow's feed_purchase_reached step. The LEDGER's delivery write is the truth and the step follows it, never the other way round, so a tap can never make the step and the ledger disagree. Idempotent on the step; a load with no workflow yet is a no-op. Registered in eventwiring.RegisterWorkflowConsumers.

events.producer: PROCUREMENT IS SOP-DRIVEN END TO END (maintainer decision 2026-09-20): procurement.Repository.CreateFeedPurchase emits ONE event per bought feed load, INSIDE the insert transaction, after the idempotency reservation. Deliberately a SECOND event beside procurement.feed_purchase.reached rather than a reuse of it: reached is the load ARRIVING (its consequence is stock and the toxin test), recorded is the load being BOUGHT (its consequence is the work owed on it). A load bought today and reaching on Friday emits both, three days apart, and each consumer reads the one it means. Payload: feed_purchase_id, park_id (resolved by the insert), farm_label, feed_item_key/label, vendor, batch_no, purchase_date, quantity_kg, already_reached. Idempotency key = 'feed-purchase-recorded:' + the record's own key.

consumers.notes: FeedPurchaseRecordedWorkflowHandler opens the load's purchase workflow: OpenSubjectWorkflow(template feed_purchase_intake, subject_ref_id = the feed_purchases row, park from the payload, NO animal), compiled from the tenant's PUBLISHED procurement.feed_purchase_intake SOP track and pinned to that version, every step stamped with its designation. Idempotent on (tenant, template_key, subject_ref_id). Registered in eventwiring.RegisterWorkflowConsumers.

events.producer: PROCUREMENT IS SOP-DRIVEN END TO END (maintainer decision 2026-09-20): toxin.Repository.RecordVerdict emits this from INSIDE the verdict transaction, on an ACCEPT only. The toxin module announced nothing before this, so no other part of the farm could tell whether a load had been screened. A rejected or Invalid round cancels itself and mints a retest in the same transaction, so the load is still owed a test and NOTHING is announced -- announcing a reject would invite a consumer to read 'we looked at it' as 'it is done'. The strip OUTCOME rides along because an accepted POSITIVE is a real result that flags the load without blocking feeding. Payload: toxin_task_id, feed_purchase_id, round_no, outcome, farm_label, feed_item_key/label, vendor, batch_no, accepted_at. Idempotency key = 'toxin-accepted:' + the verdict's own key.

consumers.notes: ToxinTestAcceptedWorkflowHandler completes the feed purchase workflow's toxin_test_accepted step for the load the round belongs to. This IS the mapping between the toxin module and the purchase: the round keeps its own state machine, retests and CEO-only verdict, and the purchase's step simply records that the load has been screened. Idempotent on the step; a load with no workflow, or an event naming no load, is a no-op. Registered in eventwiring.RegisterWorkflowConsumers.

events.producer: workforce CreateLeaveRequest write transaction: the outbox emit rides the same transaction as the request insert and its idempotency completion; the approver member ids (park_head grants scoped to the requester's park, tenant hr grants) are resolved inside that transaction and carried on the payload.

consumers.notes: One FCM push per approver device (park head of the requester's park + every hr holder), resolved by member id through the roster device registry, idempotent on workforce.leave.requested:<leave_request_id>. Maintainer decision 2026-09-10.

events.producer: workforce DecideLeaveRequest write transaction, emitted only when the LAST required slot approves: the same transaction writes the slot decision, flips status to approved and mirrors one workforce_absences row (status approved, no replacement).

consumers.notes: One FCM push to the requester (member id -> device registry) naming the window and who approved, idempotent on workforce.leave.approved:<leave_request_id>:<event_id>.

events.producer: workforce DecideLeaveRequest write transaction, emitted when EITHER slot rejects: the slot decision and the final status flip commit together.

consumers.notes: One FCM push to the requester naming the window, the rejecting slot, the decider and the reason, idempotent on workforce.leave.rejected:<leave_request_id>:<event_id>.

events.producer: workforce WithdrawLeaveRequest write transaction: the requester's own withdrawal of a pending request, committed with the status flip.
events.consumerNote: A withdrawal is the requester's own act; nobody is pushed. The Clock screen and the People / HRMS list read the row status directly.

events.producer: leadershiptasks Raise write transaction: the outbox emit rides the same transaction as the task insert, its number mint and its attachment rows, so a committed task always announces itself and a rolled-back one never does.

consumers.notes: One FCM push to the CXO the task is addressed to (resolved by user id through the roster device registry), idempotent on leadership_task.raised:<task_id>. Maintainer decision 2026-09-04.

events.producer: leadershiptasks ChangeStatus write transaction (assignee moves open/in_progress/done, raiser cancels), emitted under the row lock with the previous status in the payload.

consumers.notes: Only a move to done pushes, back to the director who raised the task, keyed on the event id so a done/reopen/done cycle is each its own message; every other transition is consumed as a no-op by design.

events.producer: leadershiptasks SetComment write transaction (maintainer instruction 2026-09-18): emitted under the task's row lock, in the SAME transaction as the note insert, its resolved @-mention rows and the participant grants each mention creates, so a committed note always announces itself and a rolled-back one never does. Emitted ONLY when a note was actually written -- a comment call that wrote no words (an older phone clearing the assignee field) is not news and emits nothing. The payload carries note_id, a note_excerpt for the push copy, and mentioned_user_ids ALREADY VALIDATED under that row lock against domain.Task.CanRead, so no consumer ever re-decides who may hear about the task. Idempotency key = leadership_task.commented:<request idempotency key>.

consumers.notes: Two FCM pushes at most, over DISJOINT recipient sets so one person can never receive both: leadership_task_mentioned to whoever the note named (keyed leadership_task.commented:<note_id>:mention) and leadership_task_commented to the task's OTHER party (keyed leadership_task.commented:<note_id>:party). The author is never notified of their own note, a self-mention notifies nobody, and the mention wins the overlap because its copy is the more specific. Keyed on the NOTE id rather than the event id, so at-least-once redelivery lands exactly one row per person per note. Deliberately bypasses the per-designation audience matrix: a mention is person-directed and must not be silenceable by job title.

events.consumerNote: A mention also records the mentioned person as a participant of that one task (migration 000346), which is what entitles them to OPEN the task the push deep-links to instead of reading a 404. The grant is direct-open only: no list scope admits participants.

events.producer: leadershiptasks Edit write transaction (maintainer instruction 2026-09-18): the raiser's change to the brief, the deadline or the attachment list, emitted under the row lock inside the same transaction as the update and the attachment replace, after the row-version fence has passed. Idempotency key = leadership_task.updated:<request idempotency key>, so an edit replayed by a retrying phone announces itself once.

consumers.notes: One leadership_task_updated push to the task's OTHER party -- the person who made the change is never told about it. Keyed leadership_task.updated:<task_id>:<event_id> because a task can be edited many times and each edit is its own news, while a redelivery of one edit carries the same event id and lands nothing extra. Bypasses the per-designation audience matrix for the same reason as leadership_task.commented: it is addressed to the two people the task is between, not to a desk.

events.producer: sale allocation confirm (maintainer decision 2026-09-07): identity.Repository.RecordSaleAllocations emits ONE event per confirm, in the SAME transaction that inserts goat_sale_allocations and exits each animal as sold (goat.exited stays per animal for obligation/tasks/health). The payload carries the sale, the confirm instant (allocated_at), the animal total and the pen-by-pen breakdown (park/shed/partition ids + names, canonical operational_location_display, animals per pen) so the Feed Director's push needs no lookup at consume time. Aggregate/subject is the sales_deal (an opaque reference, never an FK). Idempotency key = deal + allocated_at microseconds: a sale confirmed in two halves is two batches and two events; an exact replay of one confirm short-circuits on the confirm's own idempotency row before this insert.

consumers.notes: Feed Director notice (feed_sale_reduce): names the park, every pen with how many animals left it, the sale date, and the feed day the reduction lands on -- resolved from the park's normal-workflow correction clock via feeddirection/domain.SaleFeedReductionDay (before the cutoff -> D+1, after -> D+2, no clock -> D+1). Feed Director ALONE (ResolvePositionRecipients tenant/feed_director); CEO and park heads deliberately not addressed. The feed-day REMINDER (feed_sale_reduce_reminder) is not an event consumer: kernelstages.SaleFeedReduceReminderStage reads goat_sale_allocations over a 4-day trailing window on the shared operational cadence and is keyed per confirm, gated to 07:00 IST on the feed day.

SALES SOP (2026-09-19): SaleAllocatedWorkflowHandler completes the sale workflow's sale_tag_animals step (the one engine-completed step of the sales.deal SOP; a by-hand completion is refused 409 sale_tagging_pending). Idempotent on the step: a redelivery or a second half-confirm finds it completed and changes nothing; a sale with no workflow yet (its recorded event still in flight) is a no-op and the opener stamps the step later. Registered in eventwiring.RegisterWorkflowConsumers, so the API in-process bus, kernelstages, domain-event-consumer and outbox-relay all run it.

events.producer: SALES SOP (maintainer instruction 2026-09-19, docs/decisions/sales-sop.md): sales.Repository.CreateDeal emits ONE event per recorded sale, INSIDE the transaction that inserts sales_deals (+ sales_deal_lines) and the audit row, after the idempotency reservation -- an exact replay of the record returns before this insert and a refused or rolled-back record emits nothing. Payload: sales_deal_id, sale_date, farm, park_id (the farm code resolved to its park location in the same transaction; blank when the tenant has no park row for it), buyer_name, animal_count, product_type, status, has_live_animals (maintainer decision 2026-09-25: true only when an animal-kind LINE carries a head count adding to at least one whole animal -- computed from the lines written in this transaction, never the deal-level animal_count, which legacy manure deals carry as 1). The opener reads status (a sale recorded already Deal Failed opens nothing) and has_live_animals (false leaves out the SOP's `sale_has_animals` steps: tag, loading video, gate pass; an event without the key opens every step as before). Aggregate/subject is the sales_deal the outbox validator already knows (000275). Idempotency key = 'sales.deal.recorded:' + the record's own Idempotency-Key.

consumers.notes: SaleRecordedWorkflowHandler opens the sale's workflow: OpenSubjectWorkflow(template sales_deal, subject_ref_id = deal, park from the payload, SaleHasAnimals from payload has_live_animals -- nil/absent = true; nothing opened when payload status is Deal Failed), compiled from the tenant's PUBLISHED sales.deal SOP's sales_deal track (seeded document when never authored), pinned to that version, every step stamped with the designation that does it (workflow_actions.owner_role). Idempotent on (tenant, template_key, subject_ref_id): a redelivery finds the workflow and opens nothing. Registered in eventwiring.RegisterWorkflowConsumers (every bus process). The phone reads it back by subject (GET /app/workflows/subject?template_key=sales_deal&subject_ref_id=<deal>) and lists sale work under module=sales.

events.producer: penvisits Materialize (kernel stage pen-visit-kernel): one task per pen that had vaccination or PC Care work submitted on the source business date, inserted with its audit row and this outbox emit in ONE transaction, idempotent on (tenant, park, shed, pen, source date). Maintainer decision 2026-09-07.
events.consumerNote: Produced for the audit/event spine; the morning push is NOT event-driven. It is one digest per park per business date queued by the kernel stage from the tasks that pass created (notificationbridge.PenVisitDueNotifier, event key pen_visit.due:<date>:<park>:<batch>), pushed to EVERY person the park's HRMS config names as a visitor (maintainer decision 2026-09-12), because one push per pen would be ten pushes for one morning's round.
events.surfaceNotes: frontend: no admin-web list surface by decision; the People access editor edits who visits each park. mobile: the visit renders as the LAST STEP on the parent PC Care task card / vaccination shed card (maintainer decision 2026-09-12, retiring the For me tab) and submits through the outbox.

events.producer: penvisits Submit write transaction: a configured visitor's live-camera video is validated against the proof store, the row is locked, the visitor/state rule re-run, the gate flips to pending_verification (the kernel clock stays open), audit and this outbox emit ride the same transaction under the request's idempotency key; the event's idempotency key carries the row version so a re-shoot after a rework announces a fresh item.

consumers.notes: PendingVerificationHandler consumes pen_visit.submitted and calls the pen-visit verification bridge (penvisits/adapters/verificationbridge), which maps the ONE clip to verification.CreateItem idempotently (key pen-visit-verification:<task>:<row_version>) as category pen_visit in the Preventive Care verify tab. Registered in kernelstages/bus.go, cmd/outbox-relay and cmd/domain-event-consumer beside the PC Care pending handler.

events.consumerNote: The visit video goes to the verifier (maintainer decision 2026-09-12, superseding the 2026-09-07 no-verifier rule): the parent care task closes only when every video of the chain -- removal, the work, the visit -- is approved.
events.surfaceNotes: frontend: the verifier's admin-web /verify lists the pen_visit category under Preventive Care. mobile: the visit step on the parent card reads 'Visit in review' after submit; the Verify app lists the item.

events.producer: penvisits ApplyVerified (the verification.verdict.approved consumer for pen_visits/pen_visit_task): flips the visit to completed on BOTH the gate and the kernel clock, stamps verified_by/at, and writes this outbox event in the same transaction with the parents (pen_visit_task_sources, as '<kind>:<ref>') on the payload. A reject writes no event: it flips the row to rework with the verifier's reason and the visitor records again.

consumers.notes: VerifiedHandler consumes pen_visit.verified and calls the registered ParentCloser per source kind: pc_care_task -> pccare.Repository.PenVisitVerified flips every linked PC Care task whose own videos are already verified (status completed) from work_state scheduled/delayed to completed with an audit row (idempotent; an already-closed task matches nothing). Vaccination registers no closer: its shed reads derive closure from the visit row through ForSources. Registered in eventwiring.RegisterVerificationAppliers, the ONE shared list.

events.surfaceNotes: frontend: the PC Care / vaccination shed detail reads the visit as verified and the parent as closed. mobile: the parent card's chip reads 'Visit verified' and the task 'Done'.

events.producer: penroutines Materialize (kernel stage pen-routine-kernel): one task per pen (or ONE shed-less task for a whole-park routine) per occurrence of every ACTIVE routine that raises on the business date -- calendar cadences (daily / weekly / monthly / every_n_days, never before start_date) from Definition.RaisesOn, after_work routines from the verification items created in that IST day whose category maps to one of the routine's kinds -- inserted with its audit row and this outbox emit in ONE set-based transaction, idempotent on (tenant, routine, shed_key, pen, planned date). A routine whose assignee roles nobody holds in its park raises nothing and is named in the log. Maintainer instruction 2026-09-16, revised 2026-09-17 (assign by role).
events.consumerNote: Produced for the audit/event spine; the day's push is NOT event-driven. It is one digest per ROUTINE per business date queued by the kernel stage once the routine's own IST notify time has passed (notificationbridge.PenRoutineDueNotifier, event key pen_routine.due:<date>:<routine>), pushed to the devices of every holder of the routine's roles for its park, because one push per pen would be ten pushes for one morning's round.
events.surfaceNotes: frontend: /routines lists the routines per park and the Today table of what they raised. mobile: the Routines module lists the caller's checks as cards and submits through the outbox.

events.producer: penroutines Submit write transaction: every capture is validated against the proof store (finished, tenant-owned, in-app camera, declared type matching the claimed kind), the row is locked, the answers are validated against the PINNED version's evidence, the assignee/state/count/presence rule re-run, the gate flips per the routine's review kind (pending_verification, or completed on both dimensions for review none), the auto-leave is recorded when the submitter was still checked in, audit and this outbox emit ride the same transaction under the request's idempotency key; the event's idempotency key carries the row version so a redo after a rework announces a fresh item.

consumers.name: penroutines/app.PendingVerificationHandler
consumers.notes: PendingVerificationHandler consumes pen_routine.submitted and, when the payload's status is pending_verification (a review-none routine completed on submit and is skipped), calls the pen-routine verification bridge (penroutines/adapters/verificationbridge), which maps every capture as positional media (photo/video kind per proof) and the answers as context rows to verification.CreateItem idempotently (key pen-routine-verification:<task>:<row_version>) as category pen_routine under navigation module pen_routines. Registered in kernelstages/bus.go, cmd/outbox-relay and cmd/domain-event-consumer beside the pen-visit pending handler.

events.surfaceNotes: frontend: the verifier's admin-web /verify lists the pen_routine category under Routines; /routines Today table reads In review. mobile: the card reads In review after submit; the Verify app lists the item.

events.producer: penroutines ApplyVerified (the verification.verdict.approved consumer for pen_routines/pen_routine_task, registered in eventwiring.RegisterVerificationAppliers): flips the task to completed on BOTH the gate and the kernel clock, stamps verified_by/at, and writes this outbox event in the same transaction. A reject writes no event: it flips the row to rework with the verifier's reason and the assignee does the check again.
events.consumerNote: Produced for the audit/event spine and the replay/DLQ path; a routine closes no parent (docs/decisions/pen-routines.md, open question 1: V1 no), so nothing consumes it yet. The Work Board and the /routines Today table read the completed row directly.
events.surfaceNotes: frontend: the /routines Today table and the Work Board row read Done / Verified. mobile: the card moves to the Done chip and reads Verified.

events.producer: animalpurchase Decide write transaction (CEO/CXO accept or reject on a candidate animal): the outbox emit rides the same transaction as the version-fenced decision update and its audit row, so a committed decision always announces itself and a rolled-back one never does.

consumers.notes: One FCM push to the person who recorded the animal (recorded_by user id -> device registry) naming the load, the animal, the decision, who decided and any note; idempotent on procurement.animal_purchase.decided:<candidate_id>:<event_id>. The phone also re-reads the load on open/resume, so the push is the nudge and the read is the truth.

Reconciles the shared decision step from a durable monotonic source count receipt, including decisions delivered before workflow opening. Later candidate events reopen the step and stale decision events cannot close it.

events.producer: PROCUREMENT IS SOP-DRIVEN END TO END (maintainer decision 2026-09-20, docs/decisions/procurement-sop-driven.md): animalpurchase.Repository.CreateLoad emits ONE event per opened purchase load, INSIDE the transaction that inserts animal_purchase_loads and its audit row, after the idempotency reservation -- an exact replay returns before this insert and a rolled-back load emits nothing. Payload: load_id, load_ref, park_id (resolved to the park location by the insert itself, so the consumer never re-derives it), farm_label, vendor_id, vendor_name, expected_count, recorded_by. Aggregate/subject is the animal_purchase_load the outbox validator learns in 000372. Idempotency key = the load's own Idempotency-Key.

consumers.notes: AnimalPurchaseLoadRecordedWorkflowHandler opens the load's intake workflow: OpenSubjectWorkflow(template animal_purchase_intake, subject_ref_id = load, park from the payload, NO animal), compiled from the tenant's PUBLISHED procurement.animal_purchase_intake SOP track (the seeded document when never authored), pinned to that version, every step stamped with the designation that does it (workflow_actions.owner_role). Idempotent on (tenant, template_key, subject_ref_id): a redelivery finds the workflow and opens nothing. Registered in eventwiring.RegisterWorkflowConsumers (every bus process). Read back by subject (GET /app/workflows/subject?template_key=animal_purchase_intake&subject_ref_id=<load>) and listed under module=procurement.

events.producer: Animal purchase candidate insert transaction emits the serialized load decision counts after recording each candidate, including later offline sync.

consumers.notes: Retains the newest source count receipt by monotonic revision pending + 2*decided, reopening the shared workflow decision step for later candidates. Reconciles on workflow open and ignores stale events.

allowedHerdMutationWriters.reason: canonical bulk shifting relocation producer called only by the shared Park-Head-approval + operator-completion second-gate transaction; emits per-animal goat.location.changed AND (for animals reclassified into the destination shed's cohort) goat.stage_changed into goat_identity_events and matching outbox_messages in the same transaction, consumed by obligation/app/shift.go and vaccination generation
canonical Counts shed-stage cohort correction writer; emits per-animal goat.stage_changed into goat_identity_events and matching outbox_messages for changed live animals in one physical pen

canonical Counts census-slice data-correction writer for wrongly recorded breed/sex values; audit-only by design because it corrects the register without representing a husbandry state transition or triggering downstream schedule recomputation
sqlc source for identity lifecycle commands
registered existing procurement intake/exit writer; future expansion must emit/bridge domain events
idempotent local/source seed; closeout must include HRMS, stages, generation, and sweeper
idempotent local QA seed for per-goat proof testing; not a production herd mutation writer

breed RENAME on Configuration -> Breeds keeps the denormalized goats.breed label equal to breeds.canonical_name for the animals already keyed by breed_id; a label sync inside the audited register write, never a lifecycle, location, stage or identity mutation (those stay on identity's producers)

dead offspring creates no vaccination obligation
